title: Dominic and the Thorn
premise: Wren Zhou, last apprentice of the Hollow Lantern Guild, survives by selling harmless trinkets in Corvane, a city where magic is a hanging offense. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands and whispers that the covenant binding the mortal realm to the Thornwood is failing, Wren discovers her guild's charms were never fake — they were the covenant's last anchors. Hunted by the Inquisitor Ashgrave and betrayed by the guildmaster who raised her, she flees into the Thornwood with a disgraced knight and a half-fae smuggler to reforge the covenant at the Worldroot. There she learns the covenant demands a willing sacrifice of someone who belongs fully to both realms — and as a child left on the guild's doorstep from the other side, that someone is her. In the end Wren refuses the old bargain, shatters the covenant, and forges a new one built on shared grief rather than sacrifice, paying instead with her magic and her place in either world — but gaining, at last, a home she chose.
about_author: Petra Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive by their wits and are undone by their hearts.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A day in Corvane: hawking 'lucky' charms, dodging Inquisitor patrols, hiding the faint warmth real charms give off. She pays protection coin to keep the guild's cellar hidden. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she has survived ten years by being small and unnoticed.

chapters.title: Blood on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A stranger collapses against her stall, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and gasping that 'the Root is failing' before Inquisitors cut him down. Wren escapes with the map, shaking. Emotional beat: terror and guilt — she ran while he died, and now his death is stitched to her.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knew
chapters.summary: Wren confronts Guildmaster Odell Voss, who recognizes the map and orders her to burn it. She glimpses the guild's true ledger: every charm sold was a covenant anchor, and the anchors are dying. Emotional beat: betrayal — the family that raised her has been lying all along.

chapters.title: Ashgrave Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Ashgrave's POV. A cold, methodical hunter interrogates the market, senses residual magic on Wren's stall, and begins closing the net. He is not cruel; he believes magic genuinely kills. Emotional beat: dread through the antagonist's calm certainty.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered by patrols, she is saved by Ser Ilsa Marrow, a disgraced knight once sworn to guard the old covenant and exiled when it 'failed.' Ilsa agrees to guide her to the Thornwood. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two women who trust no one.

chapters.title: Out Through the Sewers of Corvane
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A tense escape beneath the city with Ilsa and Pip, a half-fae smuggler who owes Voss a debt and hates carrying it. They lose the map's decoy copy to buy time. Emotional beat: fragile found-family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. On the old pilgrim road, the land itself reacts to Wren — hedges blooming out of season where she sleeps. Pip, half fae, recognizes what she is before she does. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear of what Wren might be.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: Voss's POV via letter, read aloud at a waystation: Wren was not abandoned; she was delivered through the veil as an infant, a living bridge between realms, and the guild raised her as insurance. Emotional beat: identity shattered — her whole childhood was a custody arrangement.

chapters.title: The First Anchor Fails
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge: a village well goes bitter, crops blacken, and refugees speak of the woods 'walking closer.' The covenant's collapse is no longer abstract. Emotional beat: rising stakes made flesh; survival now means everyone's survival.

chapters.title: Into the Thornwood
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trio crosses the veil into the Thornwood, where time pools and paths rearrange. Wren's dormant magic wakes painfully; the forest greets her like a returning child. Emotional beat: awe and homesickness for a place she's never been.

chapters.title: Court of Brambles
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The fae court offers Wren welcome with teeth: they will help reforge the covenant if she surrenders her mortal ties. Ilsa nearly draws steel. Emotional beat: belonging offered as a trap — acceptance that requires amputation.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Flashback and present: ten years ago she was ordered to let the Worldroot guardian die and obeyed, and her shame has calcified into duty. She confesses it to Wren. Emotional beat: guilt confronted; loyalty and truth begin to split apart.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. To open the sealed path to the Worldroot, Pip must trade a memory of his human mother to the river-fae. He does it without telling the others. Emotional beat: quiet heartbreak; the theme of price made intimate.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Deep Green
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ashgrave, having followed through the veil using the dead courier's blood, stalks them through the forest. An ambush costs them their supplies and nearly Ilsa's life. Emotional beat: relentless pressure; the group frays under fear.

chapters.title: The Truth About the Covenant
chapters.summary: At the Worldroot's threshold, its dying guardian reveals the covenant's origin: it was never a treaty but a leash, forged so mortals could cage the fae after an old war. Reforging it means perpetuating the cage. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — saving the world may mean saving a lie.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Campfire chapter, Wren and Ilsa. Ilsa argues to reforge the covenant anyway — order over justice; Wren can't accept a peace built on chains. Voss arrives, begging Wren to sacrifice herself as designed. Emotional beat: the central argument staged face-to-face; love pulling both directions.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Choice
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. Confronting Wren at the threshold, he sees the guardian's suffering and the truth of the leash. His certainty cracks; he lets them pass — and is struck down by the covenant itself for the mercy. Emotional beat: the antagonist becomes tragic; conviction costs everything.

chapters.title: The Worldroot
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Beneath the great root, the covenant's heart flickers like a guttering lamp. It names its price: a willing soul belonging to both realms. Wren steps forward — then stops, seeing the pattern of every sacrifice before her. Emotional beat: stillness before the climax; courage becoming clarity.

chapters.title: Breaking the Bargain
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Wren refuses the old terms and pours her bridging magic into unmaking the covenant entirely, as the fae court, Voss, and the collapsing veil converge. Ilsa holds the line; Pip spends another memory to shield her. Emotional beat: sacrificial defiance — she pays everything except her life or her principles.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. From the covenant's wreckage, Wren speaks a new bargain: not sacrifice, but exchange — grief acknowledged on both sides, borders tended jointly by mortal and fae hands. The veil steadies, thinner but honest. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won hope.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POVs. Wren is magic-less and belongs nowhere formally — yet the fae court grants her guest-right, Ilsa takes a new oath to her, and Pip chooses to remember her over his recovered past. Voss returns to rebuild the guild honestly. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting; every loss named and honored.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Years later, Wren runs a stall again — this time openly selling charms at the border town of Dominic's Ford, where the veil is crossed freely. A child asks if the thorn rose really walks. Wren smiles: 'Only when it's needed.' Emotional beat: belonging finally chosen, not inherited; the price paid was worth it.
